newsitem.title: USA: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in June.

text.p: Consumer prices rose a scant 0.1 percent for the fourth month in a row in June, advancing at their slowest pace in 11 years during the first half of the year, the Labor Department said on Wednesday.

The so-called core rate of inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, also rose only 0.1 percent last month, the department said. In the first half of 1997, the core rate rose at its slowest pace in 32 years, it said.
